identification.name: Stainless Steel 316L (DMLS)
identification.common_form_notes: Supplied as gas-atomised powder for direct metal laser sintering (DMLS/SLM), printed into near-net-shape parts then post-machined as needed. See the wrought Stainless Steel 316 (Annealed) entry in this database for conventional bar/sheet/tube stock.
identification.notes: Mechanical properties are from a Proto Labs 316L DMLS (Direct Metal Laser Sintering) datasheet (a real, commonly-used metal AM (additive manufacturing) service bureau). Unlike Maraging 300 and 17-4 PH also in this database, 316L is a standard austenitic stainless steel with no precipitation-hardening response — there is no annealed-vs-aged condition ambiguity here; as-printed (typically stress-relieved, not age-hardened) is the normal final-use state, matching how wrought 316L is universally used in the annealed condition. Elongation (30%) is good for an AM stainless steel — 316L is known for retaining reasonable ductility after printing, unlike some AM alloys that become quite brittle. Bulk/condition-independent physical properties (density, Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, CTE (coefficient of thermal expansion), thermal conductivity, specific heat, melting point, electrical conductivity, usable temperature range) are reused from the wrought Stainless Steel 316 (Annealed) entry in this database, since the Proto Labs datasheet doesn't report them and they aren't expected to vary meaningfully between wrought and AM processing of the same base alloy. AM porosity for well-processed 316L is typically very low (>99.5% dense on modern systems), though no specific porosity figure was given in this source. Shear strength derived via von Mises: UTS (ultimate tensile strength)/√3 = 483/1.732 ≈ 279 MPa.

typical_usage: DMLS/SLM-printed parts needing 316L's corrosion resistance (marine, medical, food/chemical processing) combined with AM geometric freedom: custom brackets and fittings, internal fluid channels, and lightweight lattice/topology-optimized structures not achievable with wrought stock. Choose over AM AlSi10Mg when corrosion resistance and higher strength/stiffness matter more than low weight; choose a wrought 316 form instead for simple geometries where AM's cost/lead-time premium isn't justified.
